summary: This release uses stock OMP v18.12.5 as its engineering baseline. The 44 changelog entries below record the changes since v0.8.0. Historical receipts do not qualify these bytes.
highlights:
- This release uses stock OMP v18.12.5 as its engineering baseline. The 44 changelog entries below record the changes since v0.8.0. Historical receipts do not qualify these bytes.
- Opt-in **New session** creation in Tern from administrator-approved project, working-copy, and profile choices on the execution host, with durable identity-scoped idempotency, lossless local block/pane and basename correlation, OMP-native adoption into **Control**, conservative interrupted/unknown outcome handling, and automatic `tern` removal on rollback with `<configDir>/config.pre-rollback.json` backup ([ADR-043](docs/DECISIONS.md#adr-043--opt-in-tern-creation-with-omp-native-adoption)). The PWA's **Create and open Control** wizard shows progress as three steps, replays a lost-acknowledgement request only within one hour, and never recreates on an uncertain outcome. Embedded sessions report snapshot progress (`Joining session… 43%` / `Reconnecting… 43%`) in the connection status chip and accept an optional memory-only **First task** draft once into an empty writable Control composer without auto-sending; native **Open in Tern** handoff remains upstream-blocked on Android ([tern-sdk #143](https://github.com/stencil-hq/tern-sdk/issues/143)) and deferred on desktop.
- Resumable, skippable first-run trays for connection facts, optional background alerts, and View versus Control, reusing the existing tray and notification control. The bounded `omp.sessions.first-run.v1` record stores only step and timestamp. A same-scope queue clearance gets one emerald all-clear arrival, mirrored by the shell's answered check draw-in; fresh loads, routine refreshes, scope changes and reduced motion remain still (ADR-042).
- Unify Settings, Troubleshooting, Hide/Undo and request Options in one native tray system. Open request connects inside an amber tray and expands into the same live session without replacing its client, socket or composer draft. Nested focus/back, grip dismissal, safe areas, paused Undo expiry and reduced-motion paths share one implementation (ADR-041). Requests use one session-identity header and a flat client frame; Undo is a compact tile/copy/action notice, and the hero's quiet Options chip is visibly tappable. Keep successive requests coordinated with expansion and cancellation, let foreground choices supersede background resume, and return keyboard focus to the request after closing its tray.
- Document same-uid/private-ACL discovery for isolated OMP HOMEs and the unchanged 18.12.5→18.12.6 collaboration contract; extend the local lifecycle proof with native-executable publication, real View/Control attach, restart and OMP-owned revocation checks, without changing the engineering baseline lock.
- Give every session the identity Tern shows for it: a light tile holding the title's leading Nerd Font icon (or a monogram) with the session state as a corner badge, two-line titles, and a metadata line of whole facts (project · state · uptime with day units · model) that wraps between facts instead of truncating each one; hosts appear only while several are in view, the host picker becomes one compact scope control, `Hide` becomes an icon-only control with the same accessible name, and incomplete host coverage shows an amber dot.
- Move between the directory and a session with a shared-axis slide in which the tapped tile becomes the session header's tile, and move rows when a session changes group, is hidden, or returns, with the heading cross-fading between `Sessions` and `Needs you` — Material emphasized curves, 200–400 ms, typed same-document view transitions gated on a structural signature so a routine refresh never animates; `prefers-reduced-motion` and unsupported browsers render the same DOM without motion; a row keeps its tile and facts while its session opens (ADR-040).
- Show one connection-interruption story in the directory banner, reserve host rows for independently failed sources, and keep routine refreshes quiet with no Retry action.
- Report host coverage as counts without repeating host names; mark cached sessions and their counts as listed rather than live, using one consistent “list as of” clock.
- Keep empty and host-filtered directories informative when coverage is incomplete, without claiming there are no sessions on an unreachable or unauthorized host.
- Remove Retry from access-denied hosts; restoring access requires an operator or identity change.
- Keep session outage names in the connection chip and recovery timing in the triage bar, without repeating the same warning.
- Show initial session joins as neutral progress until gateway/relay health reports a fault; keep the fault name visible in compact request trays as well as full sessions.
- Replace unavailable Create actions with recovery choices, distinguish uncertain creation from failure, and identify Create-and-Control as a privileged action.
- Refresh the embedded OMP client and wire pin to v18.12.6: coalesce streaming renders and parse only Markdown tails (#14728), take linear-time Markdown/math lexing (#13961, #14667), stop idle agent-drawer polling, and adopt the eval renderer rework. Vendor the pure-JavaScript marked fork without native dependencies; retain gateway capability, Ask/photo/speech, recovery, artwork, and Show earlier behavior, including coalescing-safe return-to-tail. Transcript PUA symbols use the gateway's self-hosted Nerd Font fallback; the host baseline remains v18.12.5.
- Keep failed local targets distinct from an open remote session, including Next, Hold, and withdrawn Control actions.
- Clear expired-target notices after successful list recovery instead of recreating a resolved failure.
- Restore Hold immediately when a target failure is dismissed while its list refresh is still pending.
- Build a newly opened session's title and Control action from the latest authoritative metadata.
- Show a shared empty-list clock only when the hosts' observation instants actually match.
- Preserve cross-host Next and Hold failure notices through updates from the session still on screen, until dismissal or target recovery.
- Mark target-host access denial in red, distinct from amber connection or launch failures.
- Reject an in-flight session launch when View or Control is withdrawn, including launches resumed after browser restoration.
- Keep a newer session choice authoritative even when its launch fails while an older browser restoration is waiting.
- Resume pending request previews after a browser back/forward-cache restore without reusing an old launch.
- Restore remote sessions and update their request triage even when local authorization or the local list is unavailable.
- Attribute failed cross-host Next-ask actions to the target host and refresh expired target lists without replaying a launch.
- Return failed or changed request previews to the directory without retaining an obsolete host-selection snapshot.
- Show independently confirmed remote empty lists and retain empty-observation clocks during quiet rechecks.
- Preserve local connection faults and recovery across phone backgrounding and remote-session opens.
- Withdraw local sessions and invalidate old live events after authorization denial from launch, creation, or embedded probes, not only directory-list requests.
- Keep remote expired-session and failed-launch feedback on that host instead of replacing a local fault.
- Explain withdrawn, expired, and retained-empty observations in All hosts and single-host directories.
- Restore the current directory scope after a request preview is denied or cancelled.
- Keep the named connection fault visible while retrying a failed first session list.
- Report a remote launch access denial on that host alone, preserving the local connection story.
- Keep accepted session creation attached to the same host when fleet configuration recovers.
- Distinguish an authorization-withdrawn list from an observed empty list, even after going offline.
- Keep remote observations stale and bounded while offline, and resume polling after scheduled recovery even when the browser never emits an online event.
- Give failed fleet bootstrap one banner owner and retry it when the local connection recovers.
- Preserve the last successful empty-list clock, accessible Listed vocabulary, and neutral checking copy in held queues and answer feedback.
- Render Nerd Font Private Use Area symbols in session titles with a self-hosted Symbols Nerd Font Mono subset, split into immutable, content-hashed WOFF2 chunks loaded and cached only on first use; keep ordinary text on system fonts and make no remote font requests.
- Refuse a missing Pixel Tailscale/DNS path to the configured gateway before Android acceptance navigation, with named reachability/adb diagnostics and a read-only parent admission gate that does not poison the shared Pixel lease before a mutating child has run (#430).
- Recount prepared changelog entry-count drift against `release-text.json` before qualification, preserving every bullet, the exact requested candidate and immutable release records (#436).
- Keep local 21-case visual validation required while making only Percy upload failures advisory, with visible local/upload outcomes and capability-free diagnostic artifacts. Snapshot queueing no longer claims confirmed submission before build finalization.

stableRollback: The selected predecessor is v0.8.0. Gateway rollback does not switch or restart the separately running OMP process. This release uses stock OMP v18.12.5. rollback --to selects only retained runtimes. Preserve configuration and readiness-token state; see docs/UPGRADE_ROLLBACK.md for predecessor compatibility and stopped-service recovery.

plannedBoundary: - Planned qualification: Debian 13 x86-64; macOS 27.0 (26A428) arm64 in a Virtualization.framework guest (VirtualMac2,1, ADR-033); a disposable Windows Server 2025 host (the Administrator lifecycle and a fresh standard-user install); Chrome on the physical Pixel 10 Pro, including its background-Push lane; and real iPhone, iPad, and Galaxy devices in TestingBot's cloud. Every lane must pass against these exact signed bytes before stable promotion; the plan is not evidence.
candidateRollback: The selected predecessor is v0.8.0; pruning keeps it installed as the recorded rollback target. Gateway rollback does not switch or restart OMP. Historical fork-era recovery is documented separately in docs/UPGRADE_ROLLBACK.md.
